verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Batala casting and forging units with a genuine export or non-CV order book and clean receivables; decline job-work units dependent on a single CV or government buyer.
title: Batala castings & forgings: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business is
**A Batala foundry or forging unit melts scrap or buys billets, casts or forges a part, machines it, and sells it to a tractor, auto, machine-tool or pump maker.** Cash comes in 30-90 days after dispatch, but scrap, power and wages are paid in days, so the working-capital cycle is the whole business. **Value sits in the machining and the customer approval, not in the melt.** A unit that only pours raw castings has no pricing power; one with a drawing-approved machined part holds its price. Capex is a furnace, press or CNC line, and it is lumpy. **So when a proposal lands, check the share of revenue that is machined and approved, not just dispatched.**

**Punjab's GST collections grew 9.7% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], a real local tailwind, while electricity demand grew 8.8% against India's 9.5% [D], which is neutral.** India-wide casting and forging output (NIC 24) grew 2.4% YoY and 3.4% Apr-to-date [D]. **The data-based call is Caution at 57 [D], and the news flow does not lift it.**

## Where the growth is
**Peer results split cleanly.** Ramkrishna Forgings grew revenue 54.9% YoY to Rs 1,405 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.23% and Rs 673 crore of new orders [6]; Happy Forgings carries a nearly Rs 950 crore order book, about 60% export [5], and grew Q4 FY26 revenue 20.4% on 20.6% volume growth [7]. **Nelcast, the casting peer, saw revenue fall to Rs 335 crore in Q2FY25 from Rs 362.6 crore on subdued CV demand [4].** So pursue Batala units with export-approved or non-CV order books, and avoid pure CV job-work. **Ask every applicant for their order book and its export share; if it is under 20% and the top buyer is a CV maker, decline.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the cycle, not the balance sheet.** Keep limits to 60-70% of drawing-approved order value, take the buyer's purchase order assigned, and insist on a receivables-backed drawing power. **Take stock and book-debt statements every month, GST returns every month, and electricity bills every month — power is the truest output proxy in a foundry.** Covenant a minimum interest coverage and total debt/OPBDITA; peers show 3.8 times and 3.3 times respectively as a working reference [11], and a near-nil gearing profile is achievable in this trade [8].

**Watch power bills: two consecutive months of falling units consumed means the furnace is idle, so ask for the production register.** If receivables cross 90 days on the book-debt statement, stop fresh disbursal. **Watch the rating: a BB or A4+ profile [9] is the floor, and any downgrade means no enhancement.**
watch: Two months of falling units consumed -> site visit and ask for order confirmation
Receivables past 90 days rising -> stop fresh disbursal, recall excess drawing power
Turnover falling two quarters in a row -> re-rate the account and review covenants
Downgrade below BB or A4+ -> no enhancement, seek additional collateral
